name: list_levels
title: List levels
description: List every level of every building in floor order: id, name, floorIndex, building (parentId), role (occupied storey, roof-only level or support level), child count, gradeStanding (at-grade, partly-below-grade or below-grade against the ground line and the terrain), isGroundLevel, and which one the person is viewing (isActive); groundLevels names, per building, the level at grade (levelId, whether the building names it, floorElevation, gradeElevation, floorOverGrade, seated). A roof-only level is the roof, not a storey.

name: get_walls
title: Get walls
description: Get the walls of a level: start and end in metres, length, stored and resolved height, thickness, wallType (standard, railing or curtain; standard when absent), type ({ id, label } for a known assembly preset or project wall type, null otherwise), and their doors and windows. wallTypes lists available assembly type ids and labels for add_wall.type and set_wall_type. wallFaceChains gives base-chain provenance for geometric faces a (left of start → end) and b (right): ref (authored face slot), legacy (inline spec), or default (declared fallback ref). These are not final rendered finishes: room intent, face paint regions, exterior assembly cladding and reference availability can change appearance. A chosen white or default-matching ref is legitimate; fallback alone is not a defect or a requirement to paint.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

name: get_zones
title: Get zones
description: Get the zones (rooms) of a level: name, colour, polygon and holes in metres, area in m² (holes taken out), bounding size, roomType (room when absent, porch, deck or patio), floor.drop (step-down in metres, 0 when absent; an explicit floor.elevation takes precedence), porchFraming (auto, postSize, postSpacing in metres, beamSize, postCount and beamCount of existing generated parts; null when no outdoor/framing intent), and decking (boardSize, gap in metres, direction; resolved defaults for decks or when settings exist). auto follows porchFraming.auto; absent, on for a covered porch, off for decks/patios. false leaves framing to hand edits. These names and units match set_zone_intent. Includes the unit it belongs to (unitId and unit, its name; null: common area), and floor_choices: available floor plates (key, plateId, name, current; drawn and mezzanine flags). A room shares its floor plate with adjacent rooms unless detached. Persisted wall intent is wallMaterial (string, null when absent) and wallOverrides (wallId, geometric face a or b, finish; [] when absent), not a final rendered finish: local overrides and face paint can take precedence; absent intent is not a defect or a requirement to paint.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

name: verify_scene
title: Verify scene
description: Optional whole-scene evidence: per-level content, roles (storey, roof-only, support) and the spaces its walls enclose, then every problem found, each with a type: empty levels, walls with no room or door, a space the walls enclose with no room over it (space_no_room) or with several and no wall between them (space_many_rooms), a room the walls do not close (room_not_enclosed) or with no name (room_unnamed), two rooms on the same clear floor (zones_overlap) and floor inside a covered space that no zone or stair claims (floor_unclaimed), both warnings with their area, width and place and quiet under 0.1 m² (overlap), 0.3 m² (unclaimed) or 15 cm wide, wall bodies not counting as floor, an end that stops 3-25 cm short of another wall (wall_end_short, warning: the daylight in cm, both walls named; an end that touches a wall is a joint) and a wall 0.5-6 degrees off the line of the walls it carries on from or sits between, when that moves its far end 2 cm or more off the line (wall_nearly_aligned, warning: the angle, the offset, the neighbours; a larger turn is an angle drawn on purpose and is not named), rooms with no floor or ceiling, storeys with no stair, roof levels misused, walls intersecting a covering slab or ending coplanar with its walking surface (wall_covering_slab_contact, with wallId and slabId), openings off their wall, stairs off their slab or blocked, furniture blocking a door or overlapping, a house past its lot line or in its required yards, every node field its schema rejects (schema_invalid, with its nodeId and path; valid is then false, and the level holding the node lists it as unread and is measured once it is fixed), a node kind no schema here knows, once per kind (schema_unknown_kind, info: a plugin kind), a hidden site (site_hidden). What the surfaces of a room say, each one an observation to keep when it is intended: a wet room whose walls are not tiled where its fixtures stand (room_wet_untiled), skirting in no room or on part of the wall faces of a room (rooms_no_skirting, rooms_skirting_partial), and floors and wall faces left at the default finish (rooms_floors_default, wall_faces_default). Static authored ceiling objects report transformed bounds extending above their ceiling attachment and bounds overlapping solid covering slab bands, with node IDs and measured metres; stored and derived slab holes are subtracted. Wall-mounted objects report a front oriented toward their host; static authored wall bounds report wall-body overlap and extension through the opposite face. With settled editor meshes, catalog wall bounds and large competing coplanar faces against the host or another item on the same wall are also measured within 1 mm. Hidden back-to-wall contact is not competing face evidence. These are observations, not instructions to change the scene or proof of exact mesh intersection. Bounds are measured in the owning building frame, including stacked level elevations. Unknown catalog raw bounds without meshes, animated models, unsupported attachment frames, unresolved scripted wall cuts, roof collisions, recessed slab shells and foundation volumes are not assessed. Every warning and every error arrives whole, its own measurements with it; a repeated informational finding (severity info) arrives once, with its count, its elements and a few examples. Usage findings arrive trimmed, a narrow passage as one entry for the place with the rooms it leads to, each room's turning circle and pocket as one usage_room entry; `room` (a room's id or name) returns its whole findings plus every finding naming its items, doors or windows, even when placed in a neighbouring room; `type` returns the whole findings of that kind.

type.description: One finding type (for example "usage_passage_narrow"): the answer then lists every original finding of that type, whole, and none of the other blocks of the report.

room.description: A room's id or name: the answer lists its findings whole, including passages serving it and every finding naming its items, doors or windows.

name: place_items
title: Place items
description: Place one or more catalog items (furniture, fixtures, plants, art, lights) in one call. Each assetId is a known catalog id, available from search_assets results or existing scene item data, never guessed. Positions are level (x, z) metres. An item stands on the floor of the level, or on the host it names (targetNodeId): a wall (art, a sconce: y is the height of its bottom above the floor, required; it goes on the side of the wall the point is on), a ceiling (a pendant, a downlight: it hangs flush under it), or an item standing on the floor (a lamp on a nightstand: it rests on its top; on an object built with add_object it rests on the real surface under the point, such as a porch landing, or a ceiling item hangs from the underside above it, such as a sloped vault, and the result names it in restingOn). A room, a slab or a level as the target means its floor. Each item is placed or refused on its own (asset_not_found; outside_rooms: an indoor item on the floor outside every room of a level that has rooms — garden and outdoor items may stand outside; height_required, item_too_tall, unsupported_host, host_not_found, host_not_on_level; blocks_door: a floor item standing where a door needs space, with a spot in its room that clears every door; too_large_for_room: a floor item its room cannot hold in any turn).

assetId.description: A known catalog id; search_assets can find it.

y.description: Height above the floor (metres): on a wall, of the item's bottom (required: art centred at eye level is 1.5 − its height / 2, a sconce about 1.5); on an item, a resting height you set rather than its top. Not used on a floor or a ceiling.

targetNodeId.description: The host: a wall, a ceiling or an item standing on the floor; a room, a slab or a level means its floor. Default: the level's floor.

rotation.description: Turn about the vertical (default 0). In degrees, or text with a unit ("1.57rad").

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

name: move_node
title: Move node
description: Move one node as the editor's move tool does, re-seated on its wall, ceiling, roof segment or level, and return where it now sits and whether it clamped. A door, window or wall item slides along its wall (the plan point is projected onto the wall, clamped to stay on it, and refused with opening_overlap where it would hit a sibling, unless force, like holding Alt); a ceiling item moves in plan under its ceiling, keeping its drop; a floor or free node moves in plan on its level, keeping its height; a roof piece (skylight, chimney, vents, solar, dormer) moves in its segment-local plan, the frame its stored position uses, its height staying anchored to the segment surface; a wall takes by only (its ends translate, its openings ride in their wall-local seats). to and by are plan metres [x, z]: level plan for level, wall and ceiling hosts, segment-local for a roof host. Exactly one of to (absolute) or by (delta), or rotation alone. y is a window's sill height or a wall item's bottom height in metres, and nothing else takes it. rotation is yaw in degrees for free, ceiling and roof nodes. Returns the host class and id, the node's stored position after the move (a wall: its start point as [x, 0, z]), and whether the seat clamped. Refusals: node_not_found, node_not_movable (site, building, level, zone — use move_zone — roof, roof segment, stair, derived plates and other geometry-defined kinds), move_target_required, move_target_ambiguous (both to and by, or to on a wall), move_host_missing (its wall, ceiling or segment is gone), curved_wall, wall_too_short, wall_too_low, opening_overlap, rotation_not_supported (wall-hosted nodes face their wall side), height_not_applicable, move_not_supported (an item resting on another item).

to.description: Absolute plan target [x, z] in metres, in the frame the description names for its host.

by.description: Plan delta [dx, dz] in metres from where the node sits, same frame as to.

y.description: A window's sill height or a wall item's bottom height above the floor, in metres.

rotation.description: Yaw in degrees (free, ceiling and roof nodes).

force.description: Allow a wall seat that overlaps a sibling, like holding Alt in the editor.

name: create_room
title: Create room
description: Create a room on a level from its polygon: a wall per edge, an edge a wall already runs along reusing that wall (rooms share their boundary with their neighbour), and the room zone that names it. The floor plate and the ceiling are derived from the room — never author a slab or a ceiling for it. Declare the room's doors and windows in the same call by polygon edge (wallIndex) and t along it, no wall ids needed; each is placed with add_door's and add_window's rules, and one that cannot be is skipped and listed in skippedOpenings with its code. Returns zoneId, slabId, ceilingId, wallIds in edge order (null where no wall), doorIds, windowIds. outdoor: true draws a terrace instead: separators where no wall runs, no walls of its own and no ceiling. Where the walls already enclose a room the reconciler numbered, the call names that room instead of adding a second one; where they enclose a room with a name of its own (not a number the editor gave it), it is refused (room_named_by_person) unless rename is true, which you pass only when the person asked for the rename, so a name is never changed silently. Not available in run_batch: the result needs the floor plate and ceiling derived by the host after reconciliation.

levelId.description: The level, by an id list_levels returned; an id made up from a name ("level_1", "level_ground") does not exist. Default: the floor the person is viewing, else the lowest floor.

polygon.description: The corners in order, as [x, z] in metres.

color.description: Hex colour of the room zone, e.g. "#22c55e"; omit it and the room gets a palette colour picked from its id.

wallHeight.description: Omit to follow the storey and covering-slab underside. Equal to the stored storey height also follows that plane; other values are body heights above the wall's support, including deliberately taller walls. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

wallThickness.description: Thickness of the walls it builds. Omitted, a wall against the ground on a level below grade is a foundation wall built of what the building's region says: 8 in CMU with 2x4 pressure-treated furring laid flat inside (0.241 m) in the United States and where the scene does not say where the building stands, 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (0.354 m) in Europe; the result names the region it read, a partition inside the outline is an ordinary wall; a thickness keeps the schema wall. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rename.description: Only where the walls already enclose a room with a name of its own (not a number the editor gave it): true names that room with `name` instead of the refusal room_named_by_person. Pass it only when the person asked for the rename; otherwise ask them first.

outdoor.description: true for an outdoor room (a terrace): closed with separators (the editor's Separator: a room boundary with no wall) where no wall runs, no walls of its own and no ceiling.

doors.description: The entry door and the doors to the rooms next to it.

wallIndex.description: The polygon edge it sits on: edge i runs from corner i to corner i + 1.

t.description: Position along that edge: 0 = its start, 1 = its end (default 0.5).

sidelightLeft.description: Fixed glazed light left of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sidelightRight.description: Fixed glazed light right of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

transomHeight.description: Fixed light above a swing door and its sidelights, metres; absent or 0 means none. The full cutout must fit under the wall top (wall_too_low). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

slidingStyle.description: Sliding family: patio (default) or two-track bypass closet.

width.description: Door width (default 0.9 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Door height (default 2.1 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

swingDirection.description: Which way the door opens (default inward).

style.description: Visual preset: 'panel' (default raised-panel), 'glass' (mostly glass), 'modern' (flush slab), 'paneled-glass' (glass top, panel bottom — an entry door), 'french' (two narrow glass leaves), 'shaker' (one flat panel), 'six-panel' (3 × 2 traditional grid), 'craftsman' (4 stacked vertical panels), 'half-louvered' (slats on top, panel below — closet, laundry), 'barn' (wide recessed panel). One style per room type across the home; the entry door may differ.

windows.description: Windows, on exterior edges only: not on an edge shared with another room.

wallIndex.description: The polygon edge it sits on: edge i runs from corner i to corner i + 1.

t.description: Position along that edge: 0 = its start, 1 = its end (default 0.5).

hingesSide.description: Casement or tilt-turn side hinges (default left).

openingDirection.description: Casement or awning swing toward exterior or interior, independent of placement (new windows default outward). Ignored by hopper and tilt-turn, which open inward.

tiltTurnMode.description: Tilt-turn only: tilt inward about the bottom up to 15 degrees (default), or turn inward about the side hinges up to 90 degrees.

rollerShutter.description: Roller mount (default none): box on the exterior face above the opening, or concealed with a 0.03 m lintel strip and 0.025 x 0.03 m guides inside the reveal. Concealed curtain sits 0.02 m outside the frame plane, width minus 0.05 m.

rollerShutterBoxHeight.description: Exterior roller box height (default 0.18 m); used only by the box mount. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rollerShutterOpen.description: Static roller curtain position: 0 down, 1 fully up (default 1), independent of operationState.

shutterOpen.description: Exterior shutter position: 0 closed over the window, 1 open (default 1). Leaves over 0.75 m fold into two stacked halves; narrower leaves open flat against the wall.

shutterSides.description: Which exterior shutter leaves to build (default both).

sillOverhang.description: Exterior sill extension on each side; default 0.4 times sillDepth. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sillInteriorDepth.description: Interior stool depth (default 0.06 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorThickness.description: Interior stool thickness (default 0.03 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorOverhang.description: Interior stool extension beyond casing on each side (default 0.015 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

columns.description: Panes across each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal widths; overrides the style's panes.

rows.description: Panes up each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal heights; overrides the style's panes.

windowHandle.description: Show the interior sash handle (default true).

sashGrid.description: Pane grid per operable sash (default false; columns or rows enable it).

sillInterior.description: Add a stool board on the room side (default false).

shutters.description: Exterior shutters (default none), with a 10 mm overlap lip on one leaf when both sides are present.

shutterWidth.description: Width per side, uncapped: defaults to half the opening for both sides, full opening for left or right only. Widths over 0.75 m form a bifold pair of equal halves. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

width.description: Window width (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Window height (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillHeight.description: Height from the floor to the bottom of the window (default: centred vertically on the wall). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

style.description: Visual preset: 'single' (default single pane), 'double-hung', 'triple-hung' (stacked sashes), 'casement' (two panes side by side), 'sliding' (three side by side — wide), 'grid' (2 × 2), 'tall-grid' (2 × 3), 'wide-grid' (3 × 2), 'horizontal-bands' (4 stacked bands), 'transom' (a small row over a larger pane), 'picture' (an alias of 'single'). One style for all the windows of a room, and per room type across the home.

name: create_story_shell
title: Create story shell
description: Create one level-owned building shell from a footprint: the perimeter walls. The floor plate and the ceiling are DERIVED from the rooms the walls enclose — never author a slab or a ceiling here, and never pass boundary/autoFromWalls; createSlab / createCeiling / slabElevation are recorded as room intent instead. Use once per story; do not make first-floor walls span multiple stories.

wallHeight.description: Explicit wall height override. Omit for level-plane-bound walls. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

wallThickness.description: Wall thickness. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

createSlab.description: Floor intent for the rooms inside the shell. False records hasFloor: false.

createCeiling.description: Ceiling intent for the rooms inside the shell. False records hasCeiling: false.

slabElevation.description: Walking surface of the derived plate, stored as the room's floor elevation. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

ceilingHeight.description: Ceiling height. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

name: add_door
title: Add door
description: Add a door to an existing straight wall at t (0..1 along it), or a passage with no leaf (openingKind opening: a cased opening, an arch). The door slides to stay on the wall and reports clamped. On a railing (wallType railing) it is a gap in the guard as tall as the railing, with no leaf, casing or threshold. Refused with a code, as in the editor: curved walls, walls shorter than the door, and overlapping another door, window or wall item unless force is set. Match the reference with the outline (rectangle, rounded, arch), doorType and style; what they cannot express (glass strips, a pattern of lites, carved panels) is written as a script in code, never left as not possible. Not available in run_batch: the host opening executor prepares scripted creation and rebuilds, which a batch does not prepare.

wallId.description: The wall to add the door to.

nodeId.description: Rebuild this door instead of adding one: new code and/or params (get_source provides current code when needed). Its native fields change with update_node.

t.description: Position along the wall, 0..1: 0 = start, 0.5 = centre, 1 = end.

force.description: Place it even where it overlaps another door, window or wall item, like holding Alt in the editor. Only when the person asks for the overlap.

sidelightLeft.description: Fixed glazed light left of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sidelightRight.description: Fixed glazed light right of a swing leaf, metres; absent or 0 means none. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

transomHeight.description: Fixed light above a swing door and its sidelights, metres; absent or 0 means none. The full cutout must fit under the wall top (wall_too_low). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

slidingStyle.description: Sliding family: patio (default) or two-track bypass closet.

width.description: Door width (default 0.9 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Door height (default 2.1 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillHeight.description: Rarely needed: the door's bottom above the floor the wall stands on (default 0, on the floor). Negative reaches below that floor, down to the wall's bottom, where the wall goes down beside a floor sunk under it (a garage below the house, a step in the terrain): a garage door filling its doorway down to the garage floor. It stays between the wall's bottom and its ceiling, and reports clamped. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").

openingKind.description: door (default), or opening: a passage with no leaf, framed or arched by the outline, as the editor's door panel offers.

handleStyle.description: Door handle: lever (default), lever-curved, knob, bar, or plate.

swingDirection.description: Which way the door opens (default inward).

openingShape.description: Outline of the opening: rectangle (default), rounded top corners, or arch (round top).

archHeight.description: Rise of the arch above its straight sides, within height (arch only; default 0.45 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

cornerRadius.description: Radius of the rounded top corners (rounded only; default 0.15 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

code.description: An optional module (three.js, or bpy with language) for a door (a fan grille, tracery, carved trim): the same module and conventions as add_object, with mount 'wall'. Its size is what it builds (name params width and height so the door's size controls edit them), and its cutout mesh cuts the wall. Make it open like a real door: add an `open` clip (the leaves swinging or sliding; `close` is optional, `open` reversed by default) unless it is fixed. Native fields and code are available to express the requested shape.

language.description: The code's language: 'three' (default) for a three.js module, 'bpy' for a Blender module (see add_object). On an edit it defaults to the language the object was built in.

params.description: Values for the params the module declares; on an edit, each one you leave out keeps its current value (clamped to the param's range) and a param new to the code starts at its default.

name.description: What the user would call this design.

description.description: A short description of this design, at most 200 characters.

category.description: What this design is, in one or two words.

tags.description: Up to five short lowercase search tags, at most 32 characters each.

doorType.description: How it opens (default hinged); garage types for garage doors.

style.description: Visual preset (panels only, never the size); same presets as create_room doors[].

name: add_window
title: Add window
description: Add a window to an existing straight wall at t (0..1 along it), centred vertically on the wall, or on sillHeight above the floor when given. It slides to stay on the wall and under the wall's ceiling, and reports clamped. Refused with a code, as in the editor: curved walls, railings (railing_window: a railing takes a door, a gap in its guard), walls shorter than the window, overlapping another door, window or wall item unless force is set, and a style on a window that is not Fixed (style_needs_fixed_window). Match the reference with the outline (rectangle, rounded, arch), windowType and panes (columns × rows, or a style); what they cannot express (glass strips, leaded lites, a feature frame) is written as a script in code, never left as not possible. Not available in run_batch: the host opening executor prepares scripted creation and rebuilds, which a batch does not prepare.

wallId.description: The wall to add the window to.

nodeId.description: Rebuild this window instead of adding one: new code and/or params (get_source provides current code when needed). Its native fields change with update_node.

t.description: Position along the wall, 0..1: 0 = start, 0.5 = centre, 1 = end.

force.description: Place it even where it overlaps another door, window or wall item, like holding Alt in the editor. Only when the person asks for the overlap.

width.description: Window width (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

height.description: Window height (default 1.5 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillHeight.description: Height from the floor to the bottom of the window (default: centred vertically on the wall). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

openingShape.description: Outline of the opening: rectangle (default), rounded top corners, or arch (round top).

archHeight.description: Rise of the arch above its straight sides, within height (arch only; default 0.35 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

cornerRadius.description: Radius of the rounded top corners (rounded only; default 0.15 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

code.description: An optional module (three.js, or bpy with language) for a window (a fan grille, tracery, carved trim): the same module and conventions as add_object, with mount 'wall'. Its size is what it builds (name params width and height so the window's size controls edit them), and its cutout mesh cuts the wall. Make it open like a real window: add an `open` clip (the sash sliding or swinging; `close` is optional, `open` reversed by default) unless it is fixed. Native fields and code are available to express the requested shape.

language.description: The code's language: 'three' (default) for a three.js module, 'bpy' for a Blender module (see add_object). On an edit it defaults to the language the object was built in.

params.description: Values for the params the module declares; on an edit, each one you leave out keeps its current value (clamped to the param's range) and a param new to the code starts at its default.

name.description: What the user would call this design.

description.description: A short description of this design, at most 200 characters.

category.description: What this design is, in one or two words.

tags.description: Up to five short lowercase search tags, at most 32 characters each.

hingesSide.description: Casement or tilt-turn side hinges (default left).

openingDirection.description: Casement or awning swing toward exterior or interior, independent of placement (new windows default outward). Ignored by hopper and tilt-turn, which open inward.

tiltTurnMode.description: Tilt-turn only: tilt inward about the bottom up to 15 degrees (default), or turn inward about the side hinges up to 90 degrees.

rollerShutter.description: Roller mount (default none): box on the exterior face above the opening, or concealed with a 0.03 m lintel strip and 0.025 x 0.03 m guides inside the reveal. Concealed curtain sits 0.02 m outside the frame plane, width minus 0.05 m.

rollerShutterBoxHeight.description: Exterior roller box height (default 0.18 m); used only by the box mount. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rollerShutterOpen.description: Static roller curtain position: 0 down, 1 fully up (default 1), independent of operationState.

shutterSides.description: Which exterior shutter leaves to build (default both).

sillOverhang.description: Exterior sill extension on each side; default 0.4 times sillDepth. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

sillInteriorDepth.description: Interior stool depth (default 0.06 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorThickness.description: Interior stool thickness (default 0.03 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

sillInteriorOverhang.description: Interior stool extension beyond casing on each side (default 0.015 m). In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

columns.description: Panes across each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal widths; overrides the style's panes.

rows.description: Panes up each operable sash (the whole fixed window), equal heights; overrides the style's panes.

windowHandle.description: Show the interior sash handle (default true).

sashGrid.description: Pane grid per operable sash (default false; columns or rows enable it).

sillInterior.description: Add a stool board on the room side (default false).

shutters.description: Exterior shutters (default none), with a 10 mm overlap lip on one leaf when both sides are present.

shutterWidth.description: Width per side, uncapped: defaults to half the opening for both sides, full opening for left or right only. Widths over 0.75 m form a bifold pair of equal halves. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

style.description: Visual preset of a Fixed window's panes (never the size); same presets as create_room windows[]. Fixed windows only: an operable window draws its own sashes.

name: check_collisions
title: Check collisions
description: Assess declared item footprints with a rotation-aware plan AABB test. Supports an explicit minimum clearance and reports units, source dimensions, skipped evidence, and unsupported checks. Optionally scope to one level or floor-standing items.

minimumClearance.description: Minimum free plan-space required between item footprints. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Minimum 0 m.

floorOnly.description: When true, wall-, wall-side-, and ceiling-attached items are excluded.

candidate.description: Read-only prospective furniture item. It is checked against the target level but never added to the scene.

items.description: Candidate position coordinate. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft").
Candidate declared size. In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft"). Must be greater than 0 m.

rotationY.description: Candidate yaw around the vertical axis. In radians, or text with a unit ("90°").

name: create_project
title: Create project
description: Create a browser-visible Pascal project for the authenticated user. Use this before save_scene when the user asks for a new project.

name: get_project_status
title: Get project status
description: Authoritative status/debug call for a Pascal project: editor URL, browser-visible version, latest saved version, published version, node count, and graph hash.

name: save_scene
title: Save scene
description: Save the current scene (or a provided graph) to the SceneStore. Without id or projectId it saves to the project this session is bound to (create_project or load_scene). Defaults to a browser-visible draft save so agents can iterate without creating many project versions. Use saveMode: "checkpoint" for meaningful version history.

replace.description: Write this session's scene over a project or scene it was not loaded from, replacing what that one holds.

saveMode.description: `draft` updates the browser-visible working model without polluting version history. `checkpoint` creates a meaningful saved version; it does not publish.

publish.description: Hosted Pascal: also publish this checkpoint, making it the version the project's viewers see. Only when the user asks to publish.

includeCurrentScene.description: If true, save the bridge current scene. If false, use the graph arg.

graph.description: Full SceneGraph { nodes, rootNodeIds, collections? } to save instead of the bridge state. Judged against the scene it is saved over (the session's scene when the save goes to it, else the stored scene `id` names) as apply_patch is: a roof it puts on the walls of the storey holding it goes to the level above them, said in notes, and storey content on a roof level is refused. A graph with no scene under it is saved as it is.

name: load_scene
title: Load scene
description: Load a scene from the SceneStore into the bridge. Returns the scene metadata. Throws `scene_not_found` if the id does not exist.

name: list_scenes
title: List scenes
description: List scenes in the SceneStore. Optionally filter by `projectId` and cap results with `limit` (default 100).
